_readme: PINNED SYNTHETIC PROOF for the Template Twin certification path.
Minted once on the isolated QA stack by scripts/prod-smoke/twin-ga-proof.ts
against tests/e2e/fixtures/sample-form.docx, using the live clinical models.
Committed so CI can run the REAL compile+certify path with NO model calls.
THREE model outputs are pinned here, because three model calls sit on that
path and all three are stochastic:
mappings    - the semantic-mapping PROPOSAL made at compile time.
entities    - the Layer-3 extraction over encounterText.
note        - the constrained-fill note generated from that extraction.
The note + entities pins are the mechanism PRODUCTION already ships
(pinnedSyntheticNote / pinnedSyntheticEntities, content-addressed by
encounterSha256 + templateSha256) — synthetic-test.ts reuses them whenever
both hashes match. The mappings pin is the same idea applied to the third
call, which has no in-product pin: under MOCK_AI_CALLS the proposer returns
all 80 fields as sourceType='extraction' with a NULL clinicalConcept, and
the REAL confirm step then correctly rejects every one of them.
Nothing in the certification gate is relaxed. The seeder still runs the real
compiler, the real updateTemplateTwinMappings (which re-validates every
mapping for type compatibility, practice-default law and concept presence),
the real fill -> render -> roundtrip proof, and the real certification gate.
Only the stochastic INPUTS are fixed.
CONTENT-ADDRESSED, and every hash is re-checked by the seeder before use:
sourceDocxSha256 = sha256 of the fixture .docx bytes
encounterSha256  = sha256 of encounterText
templateSha256   = structureSha256 the REAL compiler produces for that docx
The seeder also asserts the compiled field-id set EXACTLY equals the pinned
mapping field-id set. Any compiler drift FAILS LOUDLY rather than silently
falling through to a live model call. Re-mint with twin-ga-proof.ts on QA.
PHI: none. The encounter is explicitly labeled synthetic and carries no
identifiers; note/contextText/entities were read line-by-line before commit
and contain only anatomy and invented measurements. No mapping carries a
practiceDefault, so no standing clinical assertion is injected.
encounterText: SYNTHETIC TEST ENCOUNTER — fictional data, not a real patient. Bilateral lower extremity venous duplex reflux study, bilateral detailed. Clinical indication: chronic venous insufficiency with aching, heaviness and swelling. Technique: patient examined standing, with augmentation and Valsalva maneuvers. Right leg. Great saphenous vein at the saphenofemoral junction: diameter 7 millimeters, reflux 2.4 seconds. Right great saphenous vein at the proximal thigh: diameter 6.4 millimeters, reflux 2.1 seconds. Right great saphenous vein at the knee: diameter 5.1 millimeters, reflux 1.6 seconds. Left leg. Great saphenous vein at the saphenofemoral junction: diameter 8 millimeters, reflux 3.1 seconds. Left great saphenous vein at the proximal thigh: diameter 6.9 millimeters, reflux 2.8 seconds. Left great saphenous vein at the knee: diameter 5.6 millimeters, reflux 1.2 seconds. The small saphenous veins and the accessory saphenous veins were not evaluated on this study. No deep venous thrombosis identified bilaterally. The deep system is competent. Impression: bilateral great saphenous vein incompetence, left greater than right. Diagnosis: Chronic venous hypertension with other complications of bilateral lower extremities.

## Exam Metadata

This was a Bilateral Detailed venous duplex reflux study of the lower extremities. Referring physician: [not documented]. Ultrasound technologist: [not documented]. Machine: [not documented]. Location: [not documented]. Clinical indications: Leg pain (aching), Swelling, Heaviness. Diagnosis: Chronic venous hypertension with other complications of bilateral lower extremities.

## TECHNIQUE

A duplex Doppler color flow ultrasound study was performed in the upright position with and without manual augmentation of flow and/or Valsalva maneuver, documenting the condition of the deep and superficial venous systems of the extremity, including the saphenofemoral junction, saphenopopliteal junction, great saphenous vein, small saphenous vein and perforator veins, as well as the precise location and extent of the varicosities to be treated. This study documents reflux as lasting more than 500 milliseconds in either the saphenous veins or the perforator veins.

## FINDINGS

Right Leg:
The great saphenous vein was found to be incompetent, with reflux documented at the saphenofemoral junction, proximal thigh, and knee. The small saphenous veins and accessory saphenous veins were not evaluated on this study.

Left Leg:
The great saphenous vein was found to be incompetent, with reflux documented at the saphenofemoral junction, proximal thigh, and knee. The small saphenous veins and accessory saphenous veins were not evaluated on this study.

## IMPRESSION

Right great saphenous vein is reflux positive.
Right deep venous system without evidence of obstruction or insufficiency.

Left great saphenous vein is reflux positive.
Left deep venous system without evidence of obstruction or insufficiency.

Bilateral great saphenous vein incompetence, left greater than right.

Clinical correlation with the above findings is required.
